prompts.prompt: Use case: background-extraction. Edit target: the supplied photograph of one patinated bronze tripod ding. Remove only the background to make a faithful transparent RGBA modeling-reference cutout. Preserve the original frontal camera angle and slightly top-down view, proportions, full silhouette, two tall rectangular upright ears with their genuine narrow openings, oval rim and visible dark bowl interior, narrow upper scroll band, broad belly ornament band with tall nested arch/ribbon reliefs and circular features, central vertical seam, and all THREE visible legs including the partly occluded rear leg. Preserve every existing visible relief and engraved line, bronze/green patina, warm original illumination, and dark self-shading as closely as possible. Remove the orange/brown photographic backdrop, floor, and floor cast shadow, with genuine transparent space between the legs and within real openings. The interior bowl remains part of the object, not transparent. Keep a modest transparent margin around the complete vessel. Do not brighten, de-light, redesign, mirror one side onto another, add motifs, sharpen by inventing detail, complete hidden surfaces, or crop feet/ears. No text, no watermark, no checkerboard painted into pixels. Output one PNG with actual transparent background.

Use case: lighting-weather. Edit target: the supplied transparent cutout of this exact bronze tripod ding. Make a conservative softly de-lit modeling reference. Preserve the same original camera view, proportions, full silhouette, both ears and real openings, bowl interior, rim, upper scroll band, the four visible tall nested arch/ribbon crests and three lower circular motifs across the broad belly ornament band, the central seam and all three visible legs. Preserve existing engraved and raised features as closely as possible; do not invent detail or redraw the motif, mirror sides, extend hidden panels or replace the ornament with generic taotie faces. Reduce strong warm lighting, glare and broad dark self-shadow using neutral even broad illumination. Retain gentle local relief shading to read geometry, and retain natural bronze/green patina as COLOR variation rather than geometry. Remove artificial colored edge fringes especially red/yellow contamination at the left belly and feet, with clean antialiased contours. Keep actual transparent background, all negative spaces and framing. No floor, no cast shadow, no text, no checkerboard painted into pixels. This is a softly normalized reference photo, not measured albedo. Output one RGBA PNG.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: black-and-white MATERIAL FOOTPRINT mask draft for an independent pierced highpoly relief. Input image 1 is the original photograph and is the structural authority. Input image 2 is its softly de-lit cutout for visibility. Both show the SAME ding; never refer to another vessel. Extract and approximately flatten ONLY the broad main FRONT BELLY ornamental band immediately below the narrow upper scroll band and above the plain dark bottom of the bowl. Do not include ears, rim, the upper narrow band, legs, or the whole vessel silhouette. Preserve the distinctive visible sequence of FOUR tall nested inverted-U / arch-shaped ribbon crests across the front, the small paired curls at the base of the arches, the THREE lower circular features between these arches, the center division and visible hooked transitions. Preserve original left-to-right feature count and relative spacing, including outer perspective compression as appropriate; do not invent additional side/back motifs, duplicate a panel, substitute a generic taotie face, or mirror the entire design. Produce a broad strip in a landscape approximately 3:1 canvas, orthographic front view with a small pure black margin all around. WHITE means continuous solid material. The entire full-width footprint of each raised ribbon, circular feature, connecting hook, and low engraved subpanel is solid PURE WHITE: no drawn black outlines within white surfaces. A circular depression, eye-like basin, small engraved curl, or groove inside the material must stay filled white because these will be encoded in the HEIGHT map later. Keep visible original connections continuous. Only exterior background and broad negative ground deliberately opened BETWEEN major motif ribbons are PURE BLACK. This is an independent pierced interpretation of a relief on a solid bronze bowl, not a claim that the photographed vessel has physical holes. Do not make every etched line or dark photograph area a hole. Avoid isolated floating white pupils; preserve the material underneath them. Keep smooth clean contour transitions without thin jagged branches, patina specks or noise. Output one complete BLACK AND WHITE mask ONLY, not a sheet, not a render; no gray fills, gradients, metallic material, shading, outlines, fine engraving, labels, border or rectangular backing plate.

Use case: precise-object-edit. EDIT TARGET is image 1, the existing black-and-white material footprint mask. Image 2 is the original bronze ding photograph as structural reference ONLY. Keep image 1's entire canvas size, exact framing, approximate strip outline, FOUR big nested arch/ribbon crests, THREE circular medallions between arches, central division and left-to-right arrangement. Make a targeted semantic correction: this is a material-presence mask, NOT a line drawing. Fill ALL black inner areas inside the THREE circular medallions completely SOLID WHITE, including the heart-shaped dark recess and pupil-like white island: the three features must become solid white round/oval discs because their depressed basins will be encoded only in height. Also fill the narrow black internal engraved tracks inside each tall nested arch's material envelope and the tiny narrow incised curl traces in the small bottom terminals WHITE; do not cut etched lines through the object. Keep the big distinct broad negative gaps BETWEEN major ribbon groups/crests black and keep the exterior background black. Retain the original large opening geometry and all original white main-ribbon contours as far as possible. Distinguish a broad material-free gap from an incised track in a solid casting. The four high arches should now have uninterrupted white material surfaces, ready to carry nested engravings in the HEIGHT map, instead of being many hollow outlined stripes. No black painted groove lines INSIDE a white material surface. Preserve photographed connections, without a new rectangular backing plate, extra motifs or a border. No grayscale, gradients, shading, text, noise, rendered material or layout change. Output exactly one clean BLACK AND WHITE footprint mask at the edit target's same dimensions.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: technical grayscale HEIGHT map for a pierced highpoly relief. Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET and controls the material footprint, exact canvas dimensions, framing, FOUR tall arch-shaped envelopes, THREE lower circular medallions between arches, center division, main outline and BLACK void positions. Image 2 is the original photograph and is the ornament and structural authority. Image 3 is the same vessel softly de-lit for legibility. Generate ONE grayscale height texture of the broad lower FRONT BELLY ornament, in the exact same approximately 3:1 composition and size as image 1. Do not alter its layout, feature count, margins or outline. All image-1 black voids remain pure BLACK (height 0). All image-1 WHITE material is solid: give even its lowest intact surfaces a nonzero dark-gray height at least 0.18, never a black engraved groove or black eye basin. Reconstruct the photograph's recognizable nested relief WITHIN each of the four uninterrupted white arch envelopes: tiered broad raised outer arch/ribbon, middle arch and inner arch, flatter lower lands between them, narrow shallow incised tracks, small paired curls near each bottom. These nested rings are HEIGHT changes in the same intact material, NOT extra holes. Preserve the visible three circular/eye-like medallions at their original LOW positions BETWEEN the arches: a distinct raised outer rim, lower GRAY basin and readable solid raised pupil/boss, never black holes or floating pupil islands. Keep the top hooks, center split and small curl accents consistent with the photograph rather than adding a generic face. Build a convincing hierarchy and RICH continuous grayscale slope changes: firm flat platform areas, varied ridge heights, broad controlled ramps in major masses, steeper narrow bevels where appropriate, shallow gray grooves and clean small detail. Bright gray/near-white encodes highest crests; middle gray encodes secondary stepped forms; dark gray encodes intact low lands and etched depressions. Avoid uniform balloon inflation, identical ribbon heights, and uniform 45-degree extrusion slopes. Do not encode metal patina, rust, scratches, lighting, ambient occlusion, cast shadows or directional highlights as depth. Use symmetric height ramps on ALL sides, no directional lighting or rendered-metal look. Preserve only the visible source motifs; do not generate backside/circumference motifs, labels, frames, noise or text. Output only the grayscale technical height asset on black, not a shaded 3D illustration and not a multi-panel contact sheet. Height values are artistic structure estimates from a photograph, not measured depth.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Produce a flat TECHNICAL SCALAR HEIGHT FIELD, not a lit sculpture. Input 1 is the current height draft EDIT TARGET: preserve its entire motif layout, FOUR nested tall arches, THREE low circular features, visible nested engraved ribbons, lower paired curls, framing and canvas dimensions. Input 2 is the correct MATERIAL FOOTPRINT mask: its black area determines the exact 0-height void footprint; its entire white area must remain solid with nonzero height. Input 3 is the original photograph solely for motif identity. Correct only height encoding and minor void mismatch: eliminate all directional lighting, bright specular gleams, upper-edge dark shadows, dark ambient-occlusion halos around bosses, and fine metal-like texture. No light source, no material, no rendered bevel highlights. This should read as an UNLIT grayscale data image with broad clean areas of constant gray and rich smooth numerical ramps. Define absolute values on material: lowest engraved basins and shallow tracks = medium-dark gray RGB(70,70,70), support lands = RGB(100,100,100), secondary ribbons = RGB(145,145,145), broad primary crests = RGB(195,195,195), small highest features = RGB(225,225,225). Use continuous grayscale blends between those levels for varied steep/gentle real slopes; retain some flat platform surfaces, do not quantize into hard bands. The THREE circular features are entirely nonblack MATERIAL: encode solid concentric raised outer rims, lower complete gray basins and a readable solid central pupil/boss; circles at the SAME radial distance from the center have the SAME gray value at ALL azimuths. Never black inner rings or a bright upper-left highlight/dark lower-right shadow. Likewise each nested arch has clean controlled cross-sectional height slopes with equal encoded values on both flanks, not illumination. Keep all actual black voids matching input 2, including any narrow EXISTING mask openings, rather than filling them with new pillars. Every other dark engraved groove stays at least RGB(70,70,70), NEVER black. Remove speckled noise and faceted sparkle. Preserve only original detail; no additional motifs, text, frame, change of size or new holes. Output only one pure neutral grayscale technical height texture on a black background, same exact approximately 3:1 canvas as input 1. The black silhouette must match input 2.
